description: Live demo: Redis cache invalidation by keyspace scan versus a per-entity index, measured under load in Docker.

userStories.title: Compose skeleton, Redis, and the shared toolchain
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `make up` to bring up Redis and a health-checkable workspace so every later story has somewhere to land.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml defines the `redis` service on 6379 with `--maxmemory-policy noeviction --save '' --appendonly no`
Root package.json declares npm workspaces: services/test-api, services/webhook, services/benchmark, packages/cache
Root tsconfig.base.json sets strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, target ES2022, module commonjs
Makefile provides: up, down, logs, typecheck, test, seed, reset, verify
`make up` starts Redis and `redis-cli -h localhost ping` returns PONG
`make typecheck` runs and exits 0 (no services yet is fine)
README section 'Quick start' documents make up / make seed / open localhost:3000

userStories.title: packages/cache — the shared entity index
userStories.description: As a developer, I need one tested TypeScript module implementing both the index and its invalidation, so test-api and webhook cannot drift apart.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cache exports EntityIndex with: indexKeyFor, parse, register, invalidateEntities, prune
register uses MULTI: SADD, then EXPIRE key ttl NX, then EXPIRE key ttl GT — and inspects every reply tuple
invalidateEntities order is SMEMBERS then UNLINK values then SREM the observed members — never DEL the set
invalidateEntities deletes every recorded member unconditionally; it must not filter by any timestamp
All multi-key commands are batched (default 500); no spread of an unbounded array
TTLs validated as whole seconds 1..2592000 BEFORE any write
Unit tests cover: NX+GT actually sets and extends an expiry; a failed UNLINK leaves the index intact and a retry completes; SREM preserves a concurrently added member
`make typecheck` and `make test` both exit 0

userStories.title: test-api service
userStories.description: As the benchmark, I need an innocent bystander service reading the cache, so the blocking effect of a scan is observable from outside the scanning process.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /entitlement/:userId returns {userId,hit,variants,latencyMs} per docs/API.md
It reads via SMEMBERS then MGET. It never calls KEYS or SCAN
latencyMs measures only the Redis round trip, using process.hrtime.bigint()
The service opens its OWN Redis connection, not shared with any other service
GET /health returns {ok:true}
Dockerfile builds; the service is in docker-compose.yml on 3001 with a healthcheck
`curl localhost:3001/health` returns ok after `make up`
`make typecheck` exits 0

userStories.title: webhook service with both invalidation paths
userStories.description: As the demo, I need the legacy and indexed eviction paths side by side behind two endpoints, so the graph can compare them under identical conditions.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/invalidate and POST /v2/invalidate both accept {userIds:[...]} and return 202 {jobId,mode,total} IMMEDIATELY
v1 runs KEYS *::<userId>::* per user then deletes the matches — the pattern must not match the index key
v2 delegates to packages/cache invalidateEntities
Work runs in the background; GET /jobs/:id reports {state,total,processed,removed}
POST /jobs/:id/stop aborts between users and sets state to stopped
GET /health returns {ok:true}; service is in compose on 3002 with a healthcheck
An integration test seeds ~200 keys, runs v1 and v2 on disjoint users, and asserts both remove every cache key for their users
`make typecheck` and `make test` exit 0

userStories.title: benchmark service — deterministic seeder
userStories.description: As a user, I need the fixture generated reproducibly from a seed so runs are comparable and nothing large lives in git.
acceptanceCriteria: Seeding is deterministic from SEED_VALUE: the same seed produces byte-identical keys and values
Each user gets 1..3 variants; SEED_KEYS (default 2000000) is the number of CACHE RECORDS
Writes cache strings with TTL 3600 AND the matching index sets, using pipelines of ~20k commands
Every pipeline reply is inspected; any error aborts seeding and sets state failed
On completion it asserts DBSIZE equals the expected total and stores a marker key so restarts do not reseed
GET /api/seed/status and POST /api/seed and POST /api/seed/reset behave per docs/API.md
Progress is emitted over WebSocket as {t:'seed-progress'} frames at least once a second
`make seed` completes for SEED_KEYS=50000 in under 30 seconds and status becomes ready
`make typecheck` exits 0

userStories.title: benchmark service — run driver
userStories.description: As a user, I need a run to poll test-api every second and fire the eviction batch a second later, so the graph shows a clean before and after.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/run {mode:'v1'|'v2'} starts polling test-api once per POLL_INTERVAL_MS with a random seeded user id
After BATCH_DELAY_MS it POSTs BATCH_USERS ids (default 1000) to the matching webhook endpoint and records the returned jobId
Users sent for eviction are drawn from the seeded id space so they always exist
Each poll produces a {t:'sample'} WebSocket frame including latencyMs and the webhook job counters
POST /api/run/stop stops polling AND calls the webhook stop endpoint
Only one run may be active; a second POST /api/run returns 409
A client connecting mid-run first receives a {t:'history'} frame with the samples so far
Integration test with SEED_KEYS=50000 asserts a v2 run completes and emits samples
`make typecheck` and `make test` exit 0

userStories.title: benchmark service — live UI
userStories.description: As a user, I want one page with a real-time chart and three buttons so the difference is visible without reading any code.
acceptanceCriteria: GET / serves a single self-contained HTML page — no build step, no CDN dependency required to render the chart
A time-series chart updates once per second from the WebSocket, x = seconds since run start, y = latencyMs on a LOG scale
A log scale is required: the two modes differ by ~4 orders of magnitude and a linear axis makes v2 invisible
Buttons: 'Measure legacy (KEYS) eviction', 'Measure hashed index eviction', and 'Stop'
A marker or shaded band shows the moment the eviction batch was dispatched
A status strip shows seed state, key count, run mode, and webhook job progress
If the fixture is not seeded the run buttons are disabled and a Seed button is shown instead
The page reconnects the WebSocket automatically and redraws from the history frame
Verified in a browser: both runs start, the chart moves, Stop halts it

userStories.title: End-to-end verification and documentation
userStories.description: As a visitor to the repo, I need one command that proves the whole thing works, and a README that shows the result.
acceptanceCriteria: `make verify` brings the stack up, seeds SEED_KEYS=50000, runs v2 end to end, asserts the target users' keys are gone, and exits non-zero on any failure
README documents: quick start, the two runs and what each graph should look like, memory and timing expectations, and the honest caveats from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
README states that a 1000-user v1 batch is not meant to finish, and why
README links docs/REDIS-SCHEMA.md, docs/API.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/BENCHMARK-BASELINE.md
A screenshot or captured sample output of each run is committed under docs/
`make typecheck`, `make test` and `make verify` all exit 0 from a clean clone

userStories.title: test-api read path — read-through cache, fake origin, interleaving test
userStories.description: As a reader of the write-up, I need the demo to fill the cache as well as evict it, so the fill-versus-invalidation race is demonstrable instead of only described.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cache exports readThrough() and a @Cached standard decorator built on it; experimentalDecorators and reflect-metadata are NOT used
The cache key is built from service, tenant, category, entityId and a canonical (sorted-key) serialisation of the parameters, and round-trips through parse() unchanged
A miss writes through registerMany([{cacheKey,value,ttlSeconds}]), so SET EX and SADD are in one transaction
Concurrent misses for the same cache key in one process collapse to a single loader call (single-flight)
A loader that throws is propagated and NOTHING is written to Redis — no value, no index member
An authoritative negative result is cached only under cacheNegative:true (default false) with its own negativeTtlSeconds
test-api gains a deterministic fake BillingOrigin with ORIGIN_LATENCY_MS (default 150) and ORIGIN_FAIL_USER
GET /subscription/:userId returns {userId,source:'cache'|'origin',variants,latencyMs,subscription}; originMs is present when source is 'origin'; a failing origin returns 502
GET /entitlement/:userId is unchanged; test-api still never calls KEYS or SCAN

An integration test asserts: a fill in flight across an invalidation leaves value and reference consistent and the value surviving to its TTL; an invalidation after the fill removes both; an origin error caches nothing and the next call still reaches the origin; 50 concurrent misses cause 1 loader call
docs/API.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (a 'read path' section) and README.md are updated; ARCHITECTURE states the test demonstrates bounded staleness, not atomicity
`make typecheck && make test` exit 0 and `make verify` still exits 0
